explanation: With e objects and d drops, one drop covers one floor plus the ranges distinguishable if it breaks and if it survives. Update this recurrence from larger e downwards so both branches use the preceding drop count. Values saturate at the int return limit.
timeComplexity: O(d × min(e,d)) Each of d drop rounds updates min(e,d) object counts.
spaceComplexity: O(min(e,d)) Only one previous-drop row is retained and updated in descending order.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: With e objects and d drops, one test separates one chosen floor, up to F(e−1,d−1) lower floors if the object breaks, and F(e,d−1) higher floors if it survives. These branches are disjoint and cover every possible outcome, proving F(e,d)=1+F(e−1,d−1)+F(e,d−1). Descending object counts keeps both terms from the previous drop iteration.
walkthrough: With 2 objects and 3 drops, successive covered heights are 1, 3 and 6. On the third iteration, one chosen floor combines 2 lower floors handled by one remaining object with 3 upper floors handled by both objects: 1+2+3=6.
edgeCases: Zero objects or zero drops gives zero floors.
One object permits only a linear scan of one floor per drop.
The implementation saturates at the int return limit.
